speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me; I understand you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help narrow this down, how many days have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a pruritic rash appearing after a viral prodrome, specifically with a facial rash sparing the perioral area, is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth disease). REQUEST TEST: CBC with Differential. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_rash_close_up.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19. The clinical presentation of a viral prodrome followed by a facial rash sparing the perioral area and a lacy, reticular rash on the extremities, combined with a normal CBC, is diagnostic.
